<<On Mending Of Fishing Nets This Season>>

This season, fishing nets are often repaired by local fishermen who gather at rivers and streams. They use strong threads and old rope to fix torn areas, ensuring the nets stay functional. The process is quick and efficient, with each person contributing their skills. Nets are mended in the early morning when the water is calm, allowing for better work. Local communities come together to support each other, sharing tools and knowledge. The act of mending nets is more than just fixing damage—it’s a way to sustain the fishing tradition and ensure a good catch for the coming months.
